name: Destroyer
label: Merge
lede: A Vancouver kid named his band after a Kiss album he'd never heard, then spent thirty years making the wordiest, strangest, most gorgeous records on Merge, one saxophone solo at a time.

eras.title: A rock name nobody had taken
eras.text: Dan Bejar started Destroyer alone in Vancouver with a four-track and a head full of words. Within six years he'd gone from deliberately out-of-tune home tapes to a real band, a real studio and a second job writing the oddest songs on The New Pornographers' records.

q: I was kind of blown away that it hadn't been taken already.
years.h: Dan Bejar starts Destroyer in Vancouver
years.p: Dan Bejar, a University of British Columbia dropout who'd taken mostly English and philosophy, starts recording alone as Destroyer. He picked the name because it sounded like rock and roll.
years.xp:
Bejar was born in Vancouver in 1972 to a Spanish physicist father, who died when Dan was 13, and a Jewish American mother who taught Spanish. He was raised without religion.

Only later did Bejar learn that Kiss had a 1976 album called Destroyer. He told an interviewer in 2008 he'd been too out of it to know.

years.src: Wikipedia: Destroyer (band) · Wikipedia: The New Pornographers
years.h: We'll Build Them a Golden Bridge: sixteen home tapes
years.p: Destroyer's debut is sixteen lo-fi home recordings with guitars left out of tune on purpose. One song, The Pornographers, later helps name a band.
years.xp: Reviewers heard a real gift for melody under the deliberate murk. The song title stuck with A.C. Newman, who cited it among the sources when he named [[The New Pornographers|25b75a66-ce83-4db3-b136-395a3c3784c4]].

years.cap: The New Pornographers started as a side project for everyone in it
years.h: Dan Bejar joins A.C. Newman's New Pornographers
years.p: [[A.C. Newman|bb40af12-0dfd-4a53-bfe1-666a9e49dfb2]] pulls Dan Bejar, [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]] and bassist [[John Collins|17fe13d1-ca12-4e28-a7d5-0deb9f631650]] into a Vancouver side project, [[The New Pornographers|25b75a66-ce83-4db3-b136-395a3c3784c4]]. Bejar's songs become the band's wild card.
years.xp: Bejar's Breakin' the Law was a Destroyer song before it landed on the New Pornographers' debut, Mass Romantic, in November 2000.

years.h: City of Daughters: John Collins and a proper studio
years.p: Producer and bassist [[John Collins|17fe13d1-ca12-4e28-a7d5-0deb9f631650]] joins, and Destroyer records in a real studio for the first time. Drummer Scott Morgan, later known as [[Loscil|4f2c565b-ac40-4678-ba61-4fcf3b97edbc]], joins around the same time.
years.xp:
Pitchfork later spotted the wordiness that would become Dan Bejar's trademark here, while noting that not every line rewarded close reading.

Scott Morgan played drums, saxophone, clarinet and classical guitar in Destroyer from 1998 to 2002 and came back from 2005 to 2007.

years.h: Dan Bejar moves to Spain right after Mass Romantic
years.p: A.C. Newman later joked that Dan Bejar moved to Spain two months after the New Pornographers' debut came out, which is one reason Bejar was always a part-time Pornographer.

years.h: Streethawk: A Seduction closes Destroyer's first arc
years.p: After Thief (2000) brought in a full band, Dan Bejar said he hoped City of Daughters, Thief and Streethawk would play as one progression ending here. Pitchfork later gave it a 9.1.

eras.title: Rubies on Merge
eras.text: Destroyer kept changing clothes: a loose live-in-the-room record, an album built almost entirely from MIDI, then a warm full-band record that turned a nine-minute song into a singalong. Merge became the home base in the US, and a steady Vancouver crew formed around Bejar.

years.h: This Night, Destroyer's first album on Merge
years.p: Loose, under-rehearsed and cut with little studio time, This Night split critics between beautiful mess and plain mess. By 2006 Dan Bejar called it his favorite Destroyer record.

years.h: Your Blues, built almost entirely from MIDI
years.p: Nearly every backing part on Your Blues is a MIDI instrument. Dan Bejar called the sound European blues.
years.xp: The follow-up EP, Notorious Lightning & Other Works, redid six of the songs with a live band: Victoria's [[Frog Eyes|9cf2cd10-7629-488b-abc2-f9cca721383a]], led by [[Carey Mercer|bb3ec24e-b97f-446e-b397-1f5d926f30a1]].

years.h: Destroyer's Rubies turns European Oils into an anthem
years.p: Destroyer's seventh album in six years puts the band up front: Ted Bois on piano, Nicolas Bragg on guitar, Scott Morgan on drums. Live, European Oils became a cathartic peak Dan Bejar never planned.
years.xp:
Bejar told Pitchfork he'd never hit fewer notes, yet thought Rubies had the best set of vocals he'd recorded. He called the production warm, lush and focused on making the band sound good.

The vinyl carries an extra track called Loscil's Rubies, a nod to drummer Scott Morgan's ambient project.

years.h: Swan Lake: Dan Bejar, Carey Mercer and Spencer Krug
years.p: Dan Bejar forms the trio Swan Lake with [[Carey Mercer|bb3ec24e-b97f-446e-b397-1f5d926f30a1]] of [[Frog Eyes|9cf2cd10-7629-488b-abc2-f9cca721383a]] and [[Spencer Krug|2ba12d30-216e-48b2-b673-e92203bab01c]] of [[Wolf Parade|b7ddce8b-9e5c-46bd-9d33-41b134ce1a7f]] and Sunset Rubdown. Two albums follow, in 2006 and 2009.

years.h: Trouble in Dreams, the hardest Destroyer record to make
years.p: Dan Bejar admitted a scary lack of ideas going in. Ted Bois answered with string and synth arrangements instead of plain keyboard parts.

eras.title: Saxophones, soft focus, Late Night
eras.text: Recorded slowly over two years at John Collins and David Carswell's JC/DC Studios, Kaputt swapped guitars for trumpet, saxophone and female backing vocals. It was the record that finally put Destroyer in front of people who'd never heard of Destroyer.

years.h: Archer on the Beach with Tim Hecker and Loscil
years.p: Destroyer's Archer on the Beach EP pairs Dan Bejar with ambient producers [[Tim Hecker|c7ee3bc9-780c-42c0-91e9-4cd70ad692d3]] and [[Loscil|4f2c565b-ac40-4678-ba61-4fcf3b97edbc]]. The spoken-word Grief Point runs over Loscil's music.

years.h: Kaputt: Miles Davis, Roxy Music and a lot of sax
years.p: Released on Merge and Dead Oceans, Kaputt adds JP Carter's trumpet, Joseph Shabason's saxophone and Sibel Thrasher's vocals. Visual artist Kara Walker co-wrote Suicide Demo for Kara Walker.
years.xp:
Dan Bejar said he sang in a completely different way here, almost like speaking into a vacuum. It was also the first Destroyer album with female backing vocals.

The Guardian's Alexis Petridis called it an open love letter to a vanished pop era. Pitchfork ranked it the second-best album of 2011, and it made the Polaris Music Prize shortlist.

years.cap: The Kaputt tour: no guitar in Dan Bejar's hands
years.h: Destroyer's first national TV spot: Late Night with Jimmy Fallon
years.p: Kaputt brings a string of firsts for Destroyer: network television on Jimmy Fallon's show, an official music video, and Dan Bejar touring without an instrument, just singing.

q: The English language seemed spent, despicable, not easily singable.
years.h: Five Spanish Songs: Dan Bejar gives up on English
years.p: Destroyer's Five Spanish Songs EP is sung entirely in Spanish, all covers of the Spanish songwriter Antonio Luque's band Sr. Chinarro.
years.xp: The press release opened with Dan Bejar declaring the English language worn out and not easily singable. Spanish was his father's language; Bejar had lived in Spain in the early 2000s.

eras.title: Away from the Pornographers
eras.text: Destroyer was now bigger than a side gig, and Dan Bejar quietly stepped back from The New Pornographers after Brill Bruisers in 2014. The Destroyer records got bigger too: strings, then a Thatcher-era chill.

years.h: Poison Season: strings and a live band
years.p: Destroyer cut Poison Season as a live band with big string sections. Dan Bejar said it was the first record that came close to how he saw himself as a singer.
years.xp: Bejar also said he couldn't have made something this ambitious without the success of Kaputt.

years.h: Whiteout Conditions: a New Pornographers album without Dan Bejar
years.p: Dan Bejar, who stopped touring with the band after 2014's Brill Bruisers, told Exclaim! he was deep in Destroyer's next album and didn't hear New Pornographers songs in it.

years.h: ken, named for Suede's working title
years.p: Destroyer's ken borrows its name from the original working title of Suede's The Wild Ones. Drummer Joshua Wells, also of [[Black Mountain|4898b9ad-f564-4ff1-9046-b1a16dfd5200]], produced it.
years.xp: Dan Bejar described the record to Exclaim! as cold and stark, colored by Britain in the Thatcher years that he'd been reading and thinking about.

eras.title: Still boogieing
eras.text: Past fifty, Bejar made peace with his old band and kept Destroyer moving, the lineup around him now steady for more than a decade. The records got stranger and the reviews stayed kind.

years.h: Dan Bejar rejoins the New Pornographers on tour
years.p: The New Pornographers announce tours playing Mass Romantic and Twin Cinema in full with Dan Bejar back, his first shows with them in seven years.
years.xp: A.C. Newman joked that Bejar was coming and God knows if they'd get him again.

years.h: Labyrinthitis makes the Polaris shortlist
years.p: Destroyer's thirteenth album, Labyrinthitis, leans on synths and dance beats and lands on the Polaris Music Prize shortlist.

years.h: Dan's Boogie, Destroyer's fourteenth album
years.p: Thirty years in, Destroyer's Dan's Boogie draws an 8.0 from Pitchfork and a spot on the Polaris Music Prize longlist.
